mainTopic: A גט that was written but not given, and rumors about it; earlier versus later generations; and a divorced woman who spent the night with her ex-husband at an inn
overview: This עמוד opens with the last words of an answer from the previous discussion. A new משנה follows. בית שמאי say that just writing a גט, even if he changes his mind, makes the wife unfit for a כהן. בית הלל say that even a conditional גט whose condition failed does not. שמואל rules about a rumor that a כהן 'wrote a גט': she must leave, but the matter needs investigation. The investigation is whether people there use 'writing' to mean 'giving'. The גמרא then reads 'she must leave' as referring to a second husband, so that רב אשי's rule about rumors after marriage is not broken. People will not think badly of the first husband's children, because they will assume he divorced her right before he died. Next comes a teaching that the later generations are not like the earlier ones. בית שמאי were strict about כהונה, while רבי דוסא was lenient with a captive woman. Earlier generations made sure their produce was obligated in מעשר, while later ones used routes that avoided it. Here רבי ינאי and רבי יוחנן argue about whether only the house, or even a courtyard, makes produce obligated. A final משנה asks whether a divorced woman who spent the night with her ex-husband at an inn needs a second גט. The גמרא begins explaining it with רבי יוחנן's statement, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Finishing the previous answer: the right of a future second husband
steps.stepSummary: The last words of an answer from the previous discussion. The 'second' person whose right is protected is a man who may want to marry her in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means the right that belongs to a potential second husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it began on the previous עמוד. The 'right of the second' means the right of a future husband, not one she has already married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous question assumed 'the second' meant a man she had already married. The answer redefines him as anyone who might want to marry her later. The first husband cannot block that future right.

phrases.english: [It refers to] the right that is due to the second [husband].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun in the previous sugya, before this section starts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'second' was thought to be a man she had already married.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'second' is any future suitor whose right to marry her is protected.

steps.title: The משנה: does writing a גט disqualify a wife from כהונה?
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי: writing a גט and then changing one's mind already makes her unfit for a כהן. בית הלל: even a conditional גט whose condition failed does not make her unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man wrote a גט to divorce his wife and then changed his mind, בית שמאי say he has already disqualified her from marrying a כהן. בית הלל say: even if he gave it to her on a condition and the condition was never fulfilled, he has not disqualified her from marrying a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה presents a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל. The question is whether an incomplete divorce still makes a woman a גרושה for the rules of כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that merely writing the גט leaves a 'mark' of divorce, so she is forbidden to a כהן. בית הלל go to the other extreme: even handing her the גט does nothing if its condition failed. For them, only a divorce that actually took effect disqualifies her.

keyTerms.meaning: he disqualified her from marrying a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think בית שמאי say she is actually divorced. She is still fully married to him. They only say she has become forbidden to a כהן in the future.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's case: a rumor that a כהן 'wrote a גט'. That rumor matters only if writing, or what people call writing, has a legal effect.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If one wrote [a גט] to divorce his wife, and reconsidered;
בית שמאי say:
He has disqualified her from the priesthood.
And בית הלל say:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנְּתָנוֹ לָהּ עַל תְּנַאי,
phrases.english: Even if he gave it to her on a condition,
and the condition was not fulfilled –
he has not disqualified her from the priesthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: writing alone disqualifies her from כהונה. בית הלל: even a conditional giving with an unfulfilled condition does not disqualify her.

steps.title: A question sent to שמואל about a rumor that a כהן wrote a גט
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בריה דרב מנשה asks שמואל what to do about a rumor that a כהן wrote a גט for his wife, who still lives with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף son of רב מנשה from דויל sent to שמואל: Let our teacher instruct us. A rumor spread about someone: 'So-and-so the כהן wrote a גט for his wife, and she lives with him and serves him.' What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a real-life question sent to שמואל. A rumor says a כהן 'wrote a גט', yet the couple still lives together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under בית הלל, merely writing a גט does nothing. So why should a rumor about writing matter? The question tests whether such a rumor forces any action against a כהן's marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: let our teacher instruct us (a polite opening for a question)
a rumor went out about him
she attends to him (lives with him as his wife)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Yosef sent,
son of Rav Menashe from Devil, to Shmuel:
Let our teacher instruct us:
A rumor went out about him –
'So-and-so the priest wrote a bill of divorce for his wife,'
and she lives under him and attends to him; what is [the law]?
phrases.notes: The worry is that he is a כהן. If she was really divorced, she would be forbidden to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מְנַשֶּׁה מִדְּוִיל, לִשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's topic of a written גט to a practical case of a rumor.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must a כהן's wife leave him because of a rumor that he wrote her a גט?

steps.title: שמואל: she must leave, but it needs investigation
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that she must leave her husband, but adds that the matter requires investigation.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back: She must leave, and the matter requires investigation.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question with two parts: she leaves him, and the case must be looked into.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל takes the rumor seriously enough to separate the couple. But he signals that something about the rumor still has to be checked. What that 'investigation' is becomes the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: she must leave (separate from her husband)

phrases.english: He sent to him:
She must leave, and the matter requires investigation.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ: תֵּצֵא, וְהַדָּבָר צָרִיךְ בְּדִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She must separate from him, pending investigation of the matter.

steps.title: What investigation? Perhaps whether a rumor can be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל wanted investigated. It suggests: whether we can cancel the rumor or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this investigation? If you say it is whether we can cancel a rumor or cannot cancel it —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what שמואל's 'investigation' means. It offers a first suggestion: whether the rumor can be cancelled. This suggestion is set up to be tested in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some places allow a rumor to be 'cancelled' if a good explanation surfaces. The suggestion is that שמואל meant: check whether this rumor can be cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)

phrases.english: What is [the investigation]?
If you say [it is] whether we cancel the rumor
or we do not cancel [it];

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הִיא? אִילֵימָא דְּאִי מְבַטְּלִינַן קָלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of 'צריך בדיקה' in שמואל's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly must be investigated according to שמואל?

steps.title: Rejected: in נהרדעא a rumor is never cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion fails. נהרדעא is שמואל's city, and there rumors are not cancelled, so שמואל would have nothing to investigate.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't נהרדעא שמואל's place, and in נהרדעא they do not cancel a rumor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the first suggestion. שמואל's own practice already settles that question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל is the authority in נהרדעא, where a rumor is never cancelled. He already knows the answer to 'can we cancel it?', so that cannot be what he wanted investigated.

keyTerms.meaning: his place (where he is the halachic authority)

phrases.english: But isn't נהרדעא the place of Shmuel,
and in נהרדעא they do not cancel a rumor!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested meaning of the investigation offered in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the suggestion that the investigation concerns cancelling the rumor.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שמואל's own ruling in נהרדעא already fixes that rumors are not cancelled, so there is nothing to investigate on that point.

steps.title: The real investigation: do people call 'giving' a גט 'writing'?
steps.stepSummary: The investigation is whether, in that place, people use the word 'writing' to mean 'giving' a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the investigation is whether they call giving 'writing'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning of שמואל's investigation. We must check whether the local people use the word 'wrote' to mean 'gave'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under בית הלל, writing alone does nothing, so a rumor about mere writing should not matter. But if locals say 'he wrote a גט' when they mean 'he gave a גט', the rumor really claims a divorce took place. That is a reason to separate the couple.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל separates a כהן's wife because of a rumor that he 'wrote a גט'. The open question is only whether in that place 'writing' is the everyday word for 'giving'. If it is, the rumor really says she was divorced.

phrases.english: Rather, [the investigation is] whether they call giving 'writing'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected suggestion with the correct meaning of שמואל's investigation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The investigation was whether the rumor could be cancelled.
steps.terutzMaskana: The investigation is whether local speech uses 'writing' to mean 'giving' a גט, which would make the rumor a claim of actual divorce.

steps.title: Why does it matter what people call 'giving'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 7. Even if people there call 'giving' a גט 'writing,' they surely also call actual writing 'writing.' So how could the investigation prove anything?
steps.simpleTranslation: And suppose people there do call 'giving' a גט 'writing.' Don't they also call plain writing 'writing'? So the rumor could still just mean he wrote it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation of what שמואל wanted to investigate. It argues that finding out what people call 'giving' would not settle anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said שמואל wanted to check whether people there use 'writing' to mean 'giving.' The challenge is that even if they do, the word 'writing' still also means simply writing. So the rumor stays unclear either way, and the investigation seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving (handing the גט to the wife, which is what actually divorces her)
Writing (writing the גט, which by itself does not divorce her)

phrases.english: And if they call giving 'writing,'

phrases.aramaic: לִכְתִיבָה גּוּפַהּ מִי לָא קָרוּ לַהּ ״כְּתִיבָה״?!
phrases.english: don't they call writing itself 'writing'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמואל's investigation was about whether people call 'giving' 'writing'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'writing' would still mean actual writing too, so finding that it can mean 'giving' does not clear up the rumor.

steps.title: If 'writing' can mean 'giving,' the rumor becomes worrying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that 'writing' still means writing. But if people there also use it for 'giving,' the rumor might mean 'he gave' her a גט. That doubt is enough to worry about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. But if we find out that people there call giving 'writing,' then maybe the rumor really means 'he gave her a גט.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The investigation does not have to prove she is divorced. It only needs to show whether the rumor could mean she is divorced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people there never use 'writing' for 'giving,' the rumor clearly means only writing, and writing alone does not divorce her. If they do use it that way, the rumor may mean he gave her the גט, and that doubt is reason for concern. So the investigation decides whether there is any real worry at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes (agreeing with part of the challenge)
The matter becomes known or revealed

steps.whatToRemember: The investigation checks whether the rumor could possibly mean 'he gave.' If it could, there is enough doubt to be concerned.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say the rumor proves she is divorced. It only says the rumor might mean that, and a doubt like this is enough to act on.

phrases.english: Yes;
for if the matter becomes known
that they call giving 'writing,'
perhaps they are saying 'he gave.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agrees with part of the challenge but shows that a doubt is enough
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The investigation seems useless: even where people call 'giving' 'writing,' the word still also means plain writing, so the rumor stays unclear either way.
steps.terutzMaskana: If 'writing' can mean 'giving' there, the rumor may mean he gave the גט, which creates enough doubt to worry about.

steps.title: How can she leave, if we ignore rumors after marriage?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's ruling that she must leave. רב אשי says we do not worry about a rumor that comes out after a woman is already married.
steps.simpleTranslation: She must leave? But רב אשי said: any rumor that comes out after marriage, we do not worry about it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the ruling itself from Step 4. Since this woman is already married, רב אשי's rule seems to say we should ignore the rumor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's rule is about a rumor that comes out after a woman is married, and he says such rumors are ignored. Here the woman is already living with her husband when the rumor spreads. So telling her to leave him seems to go against that rule.

phrases.english: She must leave?!
But didn't רב אשי say:
any rumor that comes after marriage,
we are not concerned about it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to שמואל's ruling and challenges it from another angle
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the woman must leave her husband
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב אשי says a rumor that comes after marriage is ignored, and this woman is already married.

steps.title: 'She must leave' refers to a second husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that שמואל's 'she must leave' means she must leave a second husband. For example, if she marries another כהן after the first one dies, she must leave him because of the rumor.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'she must leave' mean? It also means she must leave a second husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading שמואל's words in a new way. 'She must leave' is about a later marriage, not about her current husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a second marriage, the rumor came out before that marriage, not after it. So רב אשי's rule about rumors after marriage does not apply to it. Because of the rumor, she is treated as possibly divorced, which forbids her to another כהן.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's 'תצא' is read as 'she must leave a second husband.' For him the rumor came before the marriage, so רב אשי's rule does not protect that marriage.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer shows how timing works with rumors. The same rumor can be ignored for the marriage it came after, but still count for a marriage that comes later.

phrases.english: What does 'she must leave' mean? Also,
she must leave the second one.
phrases.notes: Meaning a second husband, a כהן she might marry if the first one dies. The rumor came before that marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads שמואל's ruling as being about a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'She must leave' means she must leave her current husband, which goes against רב אשי.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'She must leave' refers to a second husband. That marriage came after the rumor, so רב אשי's rule does not apply.

steps.title: Won't this ruin the first husband's children?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the explanation from Step 11. If she must leave the second husband because of the rumor, then people will think the children from the first husband are flawed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, you are giving a bad name to the children of the first husband!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 11. Making her leave the second husband seems to suggest she was already divorced while she was with the first husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we treat the rumor as true enough to force her out of her second marriage, people will assume the first husband had divorced her. Then she stayed with him while divorced, and any children born afterward would be considered חללים. So the ruling seems to hurt innocent children.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; introduces a problem that follows from what was just said
Spreading a bad name or damaging rumor

phrases.english: If so,
you are spreading a bad name
about the children of the first husband!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, אַתָּה מוֹצִיא לַעַז עַל בָּנָיו שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 11, which said she must leave the second husband
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 11's explanation that שמואל meant she must leave a second כהן husband
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forcing her out of the second marriage implies she was divorced while still living with the first husband, which casts doubt on that husband's children

steps.title: People will assume he divorced her right before he died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that since she is removed only from the second husband and not the first, people will explain it by saying the first husband divorced her close to his death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since we remove her only from the second husband and we did not remove her from the first, people will say: he divorced her close to his death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 12. People will not think the children are flawed, because they will assume the divorce happened right before the first husband died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People see that nobody forced her away from the first husband, only from the second. So they will think the גט was given at the very end of the first husband's life. That keeps the children of the first marriage untouched, while she is still forbidden to a new כהן as a divorced woman.

keyTerms.meaning: They will come to say; people will conclude

steps.whatToRemember: The rumor forces her out of a second marriage to a כהן, but it does not hurt the first husband's children, because people assume the divorce came right before he died.

phrases.english: Since it is from the second husband that we remove her
and from the first husband we did not remove her,
people will come to say:
he divorced her close to his death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains how people will actually understand the situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Removing her from the second husband would make people think the first husband's children are flawed
steps.terutzMaskana: Since she was never removed from the first husband, people will assume he divorced her just before his death, so his children keep their good standing

steps.title: Later generations are not like earlier generations
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports, in the name of רבי יוחנן quoting רבי יהודה בר אילעי, that the later generations are not like the earlier generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן, who said it in the name of רבי יהודה בר אילעי: Come and see that the later generations are not like the earlier generations.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins, comparing earlier and later generations. The גמרא will explain in the next step who these generations are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This statement is a setup line. It tells us there is a difference between generations, but not yet what it is. The next step identifies the generations, and that shows the difference is about how strict they were with the purity of כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and see; an invitation to notice something

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said,
in the name of Rabbi Yehuda bar Elai:
Come and see
that not like the earlier generations
are the later generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר אִילְעַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement after the rumor discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a difference between the earlier and later generations

steps.title: Who the earlier and later generations are
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains: the earlier generations are בית שמאי, and the later generations are רבי דוסא, who rules that a captive woman may eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The earlier generations means בית שמאי. The later generations means רבי דוסא, as it was taught: A woman who was taken captive may eat תרומה. These are the words of רבי דוסא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the statement in Step 14 meant. It names בית שמאי as the earlier, stricter generation and רבי דוסא as the later, more lenient one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי, in our משנה, held that just writing a גט makes a כהן's wife unfit for כהונה. רבי דוסא, by contrast, lets a כהן's wife who was taken captive keep eating תרומה, even though she might have been violated. This shows the later generation was less strict about the purity of כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who was taken captive
The holy portion of produce that only כהנים and their households may eat

steps.confusionAlert: רבי דוסא is not saying a captive woman who was actually violated stays permitted. He only says we do not assume it happened.

phrases.english: The earlier generations means Beit Shammai.
phrases.notes: This points back to our משנה, where בית שמאי say that writing a גט alone disqualifies her from כהונה.

phrases.english: The later generations means Rabbi Dosa.
As it was taught:
A woman taken captive may eat teruma,
phrases.notes: He means the wife of a כהן, who is normally allowed to eat תרומה.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Dosa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains who the generations in Step 14 refer to
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The earlier generations are בית שמאי and the later generations are רבי דוסא, who permits a captive woman to eat תרומה

steps.title: רבי דוסא's reason for being lenient with a captive woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסא explains: what did this Arab captor really do to her? Just because he touched her, should she become unfit for כהונה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי דוסא said: And what did this Arab do to her? Just because he pressed between her breasts, did he make her unfit for כהונה?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסא explains his lenient ruling from Step 15. He argues that the captor probably only touched her, and that is not enough to make her unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only actual relations with the captor would make her unfit for כהונה and stop her from eating תרומה. רבי דוסא says we should not assume more than touching happened. This is the clearest example of how the later generation was less strict than בית שמאי.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי were strict even about just writing a גט, while רבי דוסא was lenient even with a captive woman. That is the difference between the earlier and later generations.

phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa said:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה עָשָׂה לָהּ עַרְבִי זֶה?
phrases.english: And what did this Arab do to her?
Because he pressed between her breasts,
did he make her unfit for the priesthood?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי דּוֹסָא: וְכִי מָה עָשָׂה לָהּ עַרְבִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי דוסא's reasoning for the ruling quoted in Step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without knowing the captor actually had relations with her, mere touching does not make a captive woman unfit for כהונה

steps.title: Earlier generations tried to obligate their produce in tithes, later ones tried to avoid it
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה, quoting רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי יהודה בר אילעי, contrasts how earlier and later generations brought produce home with respect to מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה also said in the name of רבי יוחנן, who was quoting רבי יהודה בר אילעי: Come and see how the later generations are not like the earlier ones. The earlier generations brought their produce in through the main entrance so that they would have to separate מעשר. The later generations brought their produce in over the roofs and through enclosures so that they would not have to separate מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from the same chain of rabbis who taught the line in Step 14. This time the example of 'earlier versus later generations' is about separating מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier generations wanted the מצוה, so they made sure their produce became obligated. The later generations looked for a loophole and brought the produce in a way that avoided the obligation. The next step explains why the route the produce takes into the house makes a difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The main entranceway of a house
Fenced-in enclosures, not the house itself

steps.confusionAlert: This begins with the same chain of rabbis as Step 14, but it is a separate teaching. Step 14 led into רבי דוסא and the captive woman. Here the example is about bringing in produce and מעשר.

phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said,
in the name of Rabbi Yehuda bar Ilai:
Come and see
that the later generations are not like the earlier generations.
The earlier generations would bring in their produce
by way of the main entrance,
in order to make it obligated in tithes.
The later generations would bring in their produce
by way of roofs and by way of enclosures,
in order to exempt it from tithes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר אִילְעַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same chain of rabbis as Step 14, with a new example
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Earlier generations made sure their produce became obligated in מעשר, while later generations used routes that exempted it.

steps.title: Produce becomes obligated only when it comes in through the front of the house
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי explains that טבל is not fixed for מעשר until it sees the front of the house, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי ינאי said: Untithed produce does not become obligated in מעשר until it sees the front of the house, as it says: 'I have removed the holy things from the house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the later generations' trick worked. According to רבי ינאי, produce is only fixed for מעשר once it is brought in through the front of the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק speaks of 'the house,' the obligation begins only when the produce enters the house in the normal way. Bringing it in over roofs or through enclosures skips this. Until then, a person may snack on it without separating מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which the required gifts and מעשר have not yet been separated
The front of the house, its main entrance
'I have removed the holy things,' from the declaration made over מעשר

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yannai said:
Untithed produce does not become obligated in tithes
until it sees the front of the house,
as it is stated: 'I have removed the holy things from the house.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the halachic source that explains the practice of the later generations in Step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טבל becomes obligated in מעשר only when it enters through the front of the house.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even a courtyard makes produce obligated
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that entering the courtyard is already enough to obligate produce in מעשר, based on a different פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Even a courtyard fixes produce for מעשר, as it says: 'And they shall eat within your gates and be satisfied.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion about when produce becomes obligated. רבי יוחנן says the produce does not have to reach the house; bringing it into the courtyard is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן learns from 'your gates' that the courtyard, behind the gate, already counts. Under his view, the point at which produce becomes obligated comes earlier than רבי ינאי says.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixes, makes the produce obligated in מעשר

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute decides exactly when someone may no longer casually eat produce without first separating מעשר.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even a courtyard fixes the produce for tithes,
as it is stated: 'And they shall eat within your gates and be satisfied.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different opinion from רבי ינאי's in Step 18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Entering a courtyard already obligates produce in מעשר.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ינאי: produce is obligated only once it enters the house through the front. רבי יוחנן: entering the courtyard is already enough.

steps.title: New משנה: a divorced woman who spent the night with her ex-husband at an inn
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about whether a divorced woman who spent the night with her ex-husband at an inn needs a second גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a man divorces his wife, and afterward she spends the night with him at an inn, בית שמאי say she does not need a second גט from him, and בית הלל say she does need a second גט from him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new case. A couple is already divorced, but they spend a night together at an inn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether that night might have created a new marriage, which would require a new גט. בית שמאי say no second גט is needed. בית הלל say she needs one, because they may have had relations that night and thereby married her again.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who divorces his wife
and she spent the night with him at an inn,
Beit Shammai say:
She does not need a second bill of divorce from him;
and Beit Hillel say:
She needs a second bill of divorce from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמְגָרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְלָנָה עִמּוֹ בְּפוּנְדְּקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the topic of מעשר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: no second גט is needed. בית הלל: a second גט is needed.

steps.title: The argument only applies after full marriage, not after engagement
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits the argument about needing a second גט. It applies only to a woman divorced from נשואין. Everyone agrees that a woman divorced from אירוסין needs no second גט, because he is not used to being close with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? When she was divorced after full marriage. They agree that if she was divorced after only engagement, she does not need a second גט from him, because he is not familiar with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the argument from the last step by telling us which case it is talking about. It only applies to a woman who was fully married. If she was only engaged, everyone agrees there is no need for a second גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about a second גט comes from the fact that the couple once lived together, so they may have been together again at the inn. A couple who were only engaged never lived together, so he is not used to her and there is no worry. Because of this, בית הלל agree that she needs no second גט.

keyTerms.meaning: Full marriage, when the couple lives together
Engagement (betrothal), the first stage of marriage, before living together
They agree; here בית הלל agree with בית שמאי
He is not familiar or used to being close with her

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the משנה is saying an engaged woman needs no גט at all. She did get a גט. The משנה only says she does not need a SECOND גט after staying at the inn.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the whole worry depends on how close the couple used to be. That is why the rule is different after engagement and after marriage.

phrases.english: When? When she was divorced after full marriage;
and they agree about a woman divorced after engagement
phrases.notes: "They agree" means בית הלל agree here with בית שמאי.

phrases.english: that she does not need a second גט from him,
because he is not familiar with her.
phrases.notes: Literally, "his heart is not coarse with her." They never lived together, so he isn't used to being close with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the argument of בית שמאי and בית הלל from step 20 to a woman divorced after full marriage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The need for a second גט applies only to a woman divorced from נשואין. After אירוסין, everyone agrees no second גט is needed, because he is not familiar with her.

steps.title: The argument is about a case where she was seen having relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens. רבה בר בר חנה, quoting רבי יוחנן, says that the argument of בית שמאי and בית הלל is about a case where people saw that she had relations. His statement continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The argument is in a case where they saw that she had relations,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by defining the exact case of the argument in the משנה. It is a case where witnesses saw the woman have relations with her ex-husband. The sentence is not finished yet, so the גמרא is setting up the rest of רבי יוחנן's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just reading the משנה, we might think the argument is only about a couple who spent the night at the same inn. רבי יוחנן says the case is narrower: she was actually seen having relations with him. The next words will explain why בית שמאי and בית הלל still argue in such a case.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that explains the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is cut off in the middle. Wait for the rest of רבי יוחנן's words before deciding what each side holds.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The argument is where they saw that she had relations,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה's argument (steps 20–21) by limiting it to a case where she was seen having relations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, the argument of בית שמאי and בית הלל is about a case where she was seen having relations. The rest of his statement continues on the next עמוד.
